meta.siteTitle: Rabita: Mosque and cultural centre in Oslo
meta.siteDescription: Rabita is building a new mosque and cultural centre at Calmeyers gate 8, Oslo. We are raising 100 million kroner to build it.

hero.credLine: Central to the city and central to the faith, since 1987
hero.headline: The site is ready. Now we raise the building.
hero.subhead: Oslo Central Mosque is open to everyone – young and old, women and men. We offer congregational prayer, teaching, courses, activities for children and families, celebration of the holy days and much more. Together we build an inclusive community across generations and backgrounds, and serve as a bridge between Norwegian Muslims and wider society.

history.name: History
history.title: Founded in {year}.
history.body: The first Norwegian mosque not tied to a single nationality. In the heart of the capital we have been a gathering point for close to 40 years, for a great diversity of Norwegian Muslims from many backgrounds.

family.name: Members
family.title: {members} members. One community.
family.body: From more than {nationalities} nationalities we have built a community carried by {volunteers} regular volunteers and 30 leaders across the board and the departments, supported by an administration of 6 staff, 3 imams and a managing director.

learning.name: Pupils
learning.title: Over {students} pupils. Knowledge that builds.
learning.body: From weekend school for the youngest, focused on mother tongue and faith, to advanced courses for older students in language, Islam and art — Rabita offers learning for everyone. Through serious teaching we raise knowledgeable people with a secure Norwegian-Muslim identity.

volunteer.name: Visitors
volunteer.title: {visitors}+ visitors a week. A meeting place for all.
volunteer.body: Rabita is more than a mosque — it is a place people come to for prayer, teaching and activities, week after week. We also regularly welcome nurseries, school classes, researchers, journalists and partners who want to learn more about us. Our hallmark is “A meeting place for all”.

statement.before: Oslo's first mosque belonging to no single nationality.

building.title: The dream of one of Europe’s largest new mosques
building.lede: In Calmeyers gate 8 we are building more than a mosque. We are building an Islamic centre with a school, a library, a café, a restaurant, a youth club, a multi-purpose hall and a roof terrace across close to 6,000 square metres and seven floors. The old building has been demolished, the permits are in place and the contractor has been chosen. What remains is the last and most important part: funding the project. This is where you can help make the dream real.
building.brief: The old mosque was demolished in 2025. What replaces it is one building doing the work of five, on a 5 745 square metre plot, designed so the ground floor stays open to the street rather than turning its back on it.

money.title: Costed room by room.
money.lede: Every krone is tied to something physical in the building, and the accounts that prove it are public.
money.brief: The campaign is 100 million kroner across three phases. 26 995 179 kroner is in, which is 26 per cent, and the phase it belongs to is stated rather than implied. Rental apartments are part of the building specifically so maintenance never consumes the organisation again.

servicesIndex.title: Nikah, janaza, shahada and more.
servicesIndex.lede: Religious services, guidance, teaching and work out in the community. Every enquiry is handled discreetly.

detail.requestLede: Tell us a little about yourself and we will get in touch for a conversation.

nikah.title: Nikah (Islamic marriage)
nikah.body: Help planning and conducting the marriage ceremony.
nikah.longBody: Nikah is the Islamic marriage contract, entered into in accordance with Islamic principles. Rabita holds the religious nikah in the mosque, led by an imam. The couple must already be legally married and present a valid marriage certificate.
nikah.offerLede: We assist with planning and conducting the religious ceremony itself, once the marriage has been registered. Get in touch early and we will find a date that suits you.

janaza.title: Janaza (funeral)
janaza.body: Support and guidance in bereavement and Islamic burial.
janaza.longBody: In Islamic faith the end of a life has its own dignified frame. When someone passes away, family and community gather for the Janazah prayer — the last prayer for the deceased and a final farewell before burial. Rabita holds the Janazah prayer in the mosque, led by an imam.
janaza.offerTitle: We are here in the hardest of times
janaza.offerLede: In the event of a death we assist the family with the janazah prayer in the mosque and guidance through the whole process. Get in touch as soon as you can and we will help you onward.

shahada.title: Shahada (becoming Muslim)
shahada.body: Guidance and the ceremony for those who wish to become Muslim.
shahada.longBody: Are you curious about Islam, do you want to learn more about the faith, or do you have questions you would like to talk through with someone? At Rabita you are welcome to an open conversation with no obligation. Wherever you are in that process, we meet you with respect and on your own terms.
shahada.offerLede: You do not need to have decided anything to get in touch. Some want more knowledge, some want guidance, and some have reached the point of taking the shahada.

counselling.title: Counselling and mediation
counselling.body: Advice, conflict resolution and support in difficult situations.
counselling.longBody: Life can bring periods where conflict, difficulties in a relationship or other crises become hard to handle alone. Rabita offers confidential conversations and mediation with an imam or a female counsellor. The conversations rest on trust and are treated in confidence.
counselling.offerTitle: A confidential room for difficult conversations
counselling.offerLede: Whether it concerns family, marriage or other challenges, we offer conversations with an imam or a female counsellor. Every enquiry is handled discreetly.

hajj-umrah.title: Hajj and umrah
hajj-umrah.body: Information, preparation and guidance before the pilgrimage.
hajj-umrah.longBody: Hajj, the pilgrimage to Mecca, is the fifth pillar of Islam and an obligation on every Muslim with the physical and financial means to make the journey. Umrah is the lesser pilgrimage and can be performed through most of the year. The hajj and umrah office sits in Rabita’s own premises and is run by a committed team of volunteers with years of experience.
hajj-umrah.offerLede: Our partners at the Hajj and Umrah office give information and guidance before both hajj and umrah, and organise their own umrah trips several times a year. Get in touch to hear about the next one.

skole.title: Rabita school
skole.body: Weekend school for children and young people, teaching Arabic and Islam.
skole.longBody: Rabita’s Arabic school is a weekend school for children and young people aged 6 to 16, and one of our largest and longest-established offerings for children and families. In 2025 it had 225 pupils across 13 classes.
skole.offerLede: With us children should find a place where language, faith, identity and community belong naturally together. We put great weight on the quality of the teaching and on teachers who are academically strong and good role models.

koran.title: The Qur’an school
koran.body: Qur’an teaching for children, young people and adults, with weight on correct recitation, memorisation and understanding.
koran.longBody: Teaching in the Qur'an: learning by heart, and learning to read it correctly — tajweed. Children between 6 and 15 and adults over 16 have groups of their own.
koran.offerTitle: Learning the Qur’an, correctly and with understanding
koran.offerLede: We put weight on correct recitation (tajweed), memorisation and understanding, for children and adults alike.

kurs.title: The calligraphy and geometry school
kurs.body: Explore Islamic art and geometry through courses, workshops and creative activities.
kurs.longBody: Art and beauty have held an important place in the Islamic tradition for centuries. At Rabita we want to keep that tradition alive and within reach of new generations, through courses where traditional craft, history, precision and creative work meet.
kurs.offerLede: We offer courses in Arabic calligraphy and Islamic geometry, led by experienced artists. Open to beginners and the more advanced alike.

veivisere.title: Muslim guides
veivisere.body: Bridge-building, dialogue and sharing knowledge about Islam and Muslims.
veivisere.longBody: Muslimske veivisere is a dialogue and knowledge programme set up to counter prejudice and discrimination against Norwegian Muslims. Through school visits, young Muslim guides meet pupils face to face and speak openly about faith, identity, belonging, and what it is like to grow up and live as a Muslim in Norway.
veivisere.offerLede: Our guides visit schools across the country to answer questions about faith and identity, and to help reduce prejudice and build understanding. We also receive visits at the mosque.

norsk.title: Norwegian course
norsk.body: Free Norwegian teaching and guidance for adults who want to strengthen their language and knowledge of society.
norsk.longBody: Knowing the language of the country you live in is about far more than making yourself understood. It is about talking to your children’s school, understanding a letter from the authorities, applying for work, taking an education, following the public debate, and taking part in society on your own terms.
norsk.offerLede: We offer free Norwegian teaching for adults who fall outside the ordinary provision, focused on everyday language and taking part in society.

ungdom.title: Norway’s Young Muslims (NUM)
ungdom.body: Activities and community for young people.
ungdom.longBody: Young people need more than somewhere to be. They need community, good role models, knowledge, and places where they can develop, take responsibility and feel they belong. Norges Unge Muslimer is Rabita’s youth organisation, with a board of its own.
ungdom.offerLede: NUM is Rabita’s own youth organisation, run by and for young people. Here they meet for social evenings, camps and talks.

barn-og-familie.title: Children and families
barn-og-familie.body: Activities that strengthen family life, childhood and community.
barn-og-familie.longBody: Rabita should be a place where children too collect good memories, build friendships and feel the pleasure of being part of something larger. So through the year we run a range of activities and gatherings for children and families.
barn-og-familie.offerLede: Through the year we arrange trips, workshops and gatherings that give children and parents good experiences together, and strengthen the bonds in the family.

fosterhjem.title: Foster family
fosterhjem.body: Information and guidance for families considering fostering.
fosterhjem.longBody: There are children and young people in Oslo who for various reasons cannot live with their parents, and who need a safe and stable home. Among them are children with a Muslim background waiting for a family who can give them care, safety and belonging.
fosterhjem.offerTitle: A safe home makes a difference
fosterhjem.offerLede: Through the project Bro til omsorg we inform and guide families who want to become foster carers for children of Muslim background.

id-for-alle.title: Eid for everyone
id-for-alle.body: Open and inclusive Eid events for the whole family.
id-for-alle.longBody: Rabita invites the whole family to a day of activities, games and good spirits, for young and old alike. Eid for everyone has been held in several places across the city — among them Hersleb skole, Ekeberghallen and Rådhusplassen — and is announced afresh before each Eid.
id-for-alle.offerTitle: A day for the whole family
id-for-alle.offerLede: Our Eid celebrations bring together thousands of people from different backgrounds for a safe and festive day of shared prayer, activities and good food.

kurs-islam.title: Course in Islam
kurs-islam.body: Foundational teaching in Islamic faith and practice.
kurs-islam.longBody: Teaching in Islam for several groups. Jenter i Fokus and Gutter i Fokus cover the foundations — prayer, ritual washing and tawhid — across two age groups: 10 to 13, and 14 to 18.
kurs-islam.offerTitle: Foundational knowledge in a safe setting
kurs-islam.offerLede: The course gives children and young people a solid grounding in Islamic faith and practice, adapted to their own age groups.

kurs-konvertitter.title: A course for converts
kurs-konvertitter.body: An Islam course for new Muslims, every Friday. Open to anyone who wants to learn.
kurs-konvertitter.longBody: A course in the foundations of Islam, made for new Muslims. We eat together, and it is open to anyone with an interest in learning — including those born Muslim, and those who are not Muslim at all.
kurs-konvertitter.offerLede: The course covers the foundations and assumes nothing. You can come on your own.

offer.title: Every Friday
offer.body: The course runs weekly through the year.

offer.title: The foundations of Islam
offer.body: We start at the beginning. No prior knowledge is needed.

offer.title: We eat together
offer.body: The course has a social half. It is a way to get to know people, not only a classroom.

offer.title: Wider than converts
offer.body: Anyone with an interest in learning is welcome.

arabisk.title: Course in Arabic
arabisk.body: Arabic tuition for adults at different levels, from beginner to advanced.
arabisk.longBody: Teaching in Arabic for adults over 16, at two levels. Level 1 begins with the alphabet. Level 2 builds on it with grammar, vocabulary and reading continuous text.
arabisk.offerTitle: From the first word to fluency
arabisk.offerLede: We offer Arabic tuition at two levels, for adults who want to learn the language or strengthen it.

kvinnetreff.title: Women’s gatherings
kvinnetreff.body: Educational, social and spiritual offerings for women of all ages.
kvinnetreff.longBody: Kvinnetreff is a meeting place of its own for the women of Rabita, with room for conversation, teaching and time together. The gatherings are held at the mosque. Get in touch to hear when the next one takes place, or to say you would like to come.
kvinnetreff.offerTitle: A community for women of all ages
kvinnetreff.offerLede: With us women meet for talks, social gatherings and educational sessions in a safe and welcoming setting.

factNotes.founded: The start of our journey in Oslo

history.p1: Rabita was founded in 1987 as the first mosque in Oslo not tied to one particular nationality. The vision was simple but ambitious: to be a gathering place for Muslims in Norway, whatever their background, language or country of origin.
history.p2: Over the years Rabita has grown into more than a mosque. The school was established, the cultural and civic work took shape, and the organisation became an active contributor to interfaith dialogue, volunteering and local community development. Today Rabita is an important part of Oslo’s civil society and a gathering point for people of all ages.
history.p3: In October 2009 Rabita was visited by King Harald V and Crown Prince Haakon, the first royal visit to a mosque in Norway. Today we still work toward the same goal we set out with: to be an open community where faith, knowledge and active citizenship go hand in hand.
history.p4: As our activities have grown, the premises we have are no longer big enough to meet the need. Support the work of realising the new building, which will make room for further growth, strengthen what we offer and meet the needs of today’s generation and tomorrow’s.

projectOverview.briefShort: The old building has been demolished, and construction of our new mosque is under way. In Calmeyers gate 8 we are raising one of Europe’s largest new mosques, with a prayer hall across three floors, a school, a library, a café, a restaurant, a youth club, a multi-purpose hall and a roof terrace over close to 6,000 square metres and seven floors. It will be a gathering place for faith, learning and community for generations to come.

about.heading: Living in the heart of Oslo.
about.body1: A rare chance to live in the heart of Oslo, centrally placed and a short walk from government institutions, tourist attractions, major transport hubs and large shopping centres — and, not least, in the same building as the Oslo Mosque.
about.body2: The project comprises modern apartments and a broad range of facilities, among them a café, restaurants, a multi-purpose hall, a roof terrace and sheltered outdoor areas.

modern.title: Modern apartments
modern.body: Efficient layouts, good materials and a light design.

central.title: Central location
central.body: Walking distance to Oslo S, the Storting and the main transport hubs.

location.heading: Close to everything that matters.
location.lede: Calmeyers gate sits in an attractive, well-established part of Oslo, within walking distance of the city's most important functions.

A short walk to Grünerløkka, with its wide choice of cafés, restaurants and shops

imams.heading: The people who lead the prayer.
imams.lede: One theological leader and two imams. You meet them at Friday prayer, in the classes, and in the conversation afterwards.

amara.bio: Theological director at Rabita since the early 2000s. Educated at the sharia faculty of the University of Beirut and in pedagogy at Oslo University College. Heads the European Council of Imams, has long experience as a teacher in Norwegian schools and is a much-invited speaker in Norway and Europe. Holds overall responsibility for theological questions and rulings in the congregation.

andreas.bio: Norwegian-speaking imam since 2023. Has studied under several Norwegian imams, among them Sh. Bouchta. Delivers the Friday sermon and plays a central role in teaching, lecturing and conversations with members and visitors who speak mainly Norwegian. Speaks several languages and is known for his calm and beautiful Qur’anic recitation.

aldiri.bio: Appointed imam in 2025. Holds a doctorate in Islamic studies from the University of Jordan and broad expertise in dialogue work, youth work and communication. He is particularly committed to the development of young Muslims. Gives short reminders after the daily prayers and contributes theological guidance and teaching.

fremdrift.title: From vision to finished building.
fremdrift.lede: The most pivotal years of the project now lie ahead. The old mosque has been demolished and the ground cleared. We now begin the work of building a mosque that will serve generations to come.
fremdrift.aheadHeading: The years in front of us.
fremdrift.aheadLede: As we approach the end of 2025, we stand at a defining moment in the project. The old mosque is now part of our history. The building has been dismantled and the site has been cleared. For many years it was our shared home. Now we open the door to something greater, more beautiful and more sustainable. The first two phases have been completed. We now enter the next, and most crucial, phase: the construction of the mosque itself.

vision.name: Vision
vision.body: After many years in our former mosque, the need for a larger space became increasingly clear. The old building was worn down, expensive to maintain, and no longer met the needs of our growing community. That is why a bold new vision was launched: to tear down the existing structure and build a new, modern Islamic centre — with a mosque spanning multiple floors, a school, a library, a youth club, a multi-purpose hall and residential units.

preparation.name: Preparation
preparation.body: The first official steps toward a new mosque were taken in 2019, when we entered a long-term collaboration with architect Håvard Lindgard Fagernes, who developed the initial design sketches. In 2022 the project received full approval from the municipality, and by 2024 it was opened to bids from some of the country's leading construction firms. These milestones laid a solid foundation and marked the beginning of a new chapter: the mosque of the future.

demolition.name: Demolition
demolition.body: After several years of ideas, sketches and careful planning, the first major milestone was reached in 2025. During Ramadan that year, demolition began on the 19th-century building that had served as our mosque for generations. We carried with us the memories and stories shaped within its walls, while knowing in our hearts that this was the beginning of something new.

construction.label: In progress
construction.name: Construction
construction.body: The aim of this phase is to build the foundation, main structure and facade. This is the project’s most critical phase — a milestone that brings us closer to the vision of a new, modern mosque in the middle of Oslo.

interior.label: Upcoming
interior.name: Interior
interior.body: The aim of this phase is to complete the interior of the basement, first and second floors. These floors are the heart of the building, with prayer halls across three storeys, wudu facilities and cloakrooms.

completion.label: Upcoming
completion.name: Completion
completion.body: In the final phase, the aim is to complete the upper floors. The third floor will be dedicated to education, with modern classrooms and flexible spaces for weekend school, courses and lectures. The fourth floor will house offices, meeting rooms, a studio and a large youth club. The fifth and sixth floors will contain residential apartments, providing stable income to help sustain the mosque's upkeep and community activities for years to come.

fremdrift.goalNote: The build cost is given in euro, as it is budgeted per phase. Our fundraising is in kroner and covers a share of it — the two are not the same figure, and we do not convert one into the other.

roomDesc.prayerMain: The heart of the building. Here the congregation gathers for the daily prayers, Friday prayer and the celebration of the holy days.
roomDesc.prayerMen: The prayer room in the lower floor, with bookshelves along the walls and an open gallery above.
roomDesc.prayerWomen: Set on the gallery with a view over the main hall and direct access to the garden.
roomDesc.wuduMen: The washing places before prayer, designed so that many can perform wudu at once.
roomDesc.sportsHall: A hall for sport, training and activities through the whole week.
roomDesc.foyer: Daylight from above, the library to one side and the staircase that ties the floors together.
roomDesc.cafe: The café sits just inside the street and is open to the congregation and the city alike.
roomDesc.library: Norwegian, English and Arabic books on Islam. A place for study, learning and quiet.
roomDesc.commercial: A restaurant facing the street, with a dining room, service and a full kitchen.
roomDesc.childrensRoom: A playroom beside the prayer hall, so the youngest have somewhere to be while their parents pray.
roomDesc.imamOffice: The imams’ offices. A place for conversation, guidance and support in matters large and small.
roomDesc.garden: A sheltered outdoor room in the middle of the block, with benches, flowers and a fountain with an eight-pointed star.
roomDesc.school: Bright, modern classrooms where children and young people can learn, develop and build a secure identity.
roomDesc.conference: Flexible premises for conferences, courses, weddings and celebrations.
roomDesc.meetingRooms: Meeting rooms for the board, the administration, the departments and partners.
roomDesc.youthClub: A place for children and young people, with games, activities and somewhere to be together.
roomDesc.apartments: Fifteen highly attractive apartments, centrally placed in the heart of Oslo.
roomDesc.roofTerrace: Tables under sails, planting and a view over the city’s rooftops. An outdoor room for visitors and residents alike.
roomDesc.minaret: The minaret is integrated into the courtyard and shaped from the building’s fire stair. It draws on a long tradition in Islamic architecture and is adapted to the building’s modern idiom.
roomDesc.prayerScreened: A prayer room of its own for adults with small children.
roomDesc.wuduWomen: Separate facilities for ritual washing, designed for comfort and accessibility before prayer.
roomDesc.amphi: Steps that become seating. A place for gatherings, presentations and fresh air.
roomDesc.administration: The offices of the staff who plan, organise and keep the mosque running.
roomDesc.studio: A studio for recording and streaming lectures, Friday sermons and digital content.
roomDesc.guestArea: A room for visitors and guests, right by the staircase that ties the floors together.
roomDesc.dome: The dome is a central element of mosque architecture and stands for community, faith and belonging.
